pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How is a kayamba played? (1 mark)
   A. By blowing into it
   B. By rubbing a bow across it
   C. By plucking strings
   D. By shaking it

2. What is the job of the ropes on a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To make the shell heavy
   B. To decorate the beater
   C. To make the drum float
   D. To hold the skin tight

3. What is the first step in improvising an accompaniment to a song? (1 mark)
   A. Stop singing
   B. Buy a drum
   C. Find the steady beat
   D. Change the words

4. What does the drumhead do when it is struck? (1 mark)
   A. It vibrates and makes the sound
   B. It holds the drum stand
   C. It stays completely still
   D. It cools the drum

5. In art, tone or value means (1 mark)
   A. how big it is
   B. how light or dark something is
   C. how loud it is
   D. how old it is

6. What is the minimum distance a defender must keep from the player with the ball? (1 mark)
   A. 5 metres
   B. 1 centimetre
   C. 10 metres
   D. 0.9 metres

7. In a montage, the subject matter means (1 mark)
   A. the price of the paper
   B. the colour of the desk
   C. what the montage is about
   D. the size of the glue pot

8. What can you do to clean your working area after painting? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it messy
   B. Throw paint on the floor
   C. Pour paint in a stream where animals drink
   D. Wash brushes and wipe the desk

9. A rest is a sign for (1 mark)
   A. silence
   B. a song title
   C. a repeat
   D. the loudest sound

10. The French rhythm name for a crotchet is (1 mark)
   A. te-te
   B. sh
   C. ta-te
   D. taa

11. Which of these letters is a tall letter with an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. x
   B. n
   C. u
   D. t

12. Listening for the name of a note without seeing it is called (1 mark)
   A. drawing
   B. aural work
   C. running
   D. painting

13. Which move is a step? (1 mark)
   A. m to d in one jump over r
   B. d to r
   C. d to d
   D. d to m

14. On the Kenyan flag, green stands for (1 mark)
   A. the land and natural wealth
   B. the sun
   C. the people
   D. the rivers only

15. The shield and two crossed spears on the flag stand for (1 mark)
   A. defence of freedom
   B. sports
   C. music
   D. farming

16. The bottom stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. black
   B. white
   C. green
   D. red

17. Leaning far backwards while sprinting will (1 mark)
   A. make no difference
   B. make you jump
   C. slow you down like a brake
   D. make you faster

18. Which is a good ratio of length to height for a flag drawing? (1 mark)
   A. Three to two
   B. Ten to one
   C. One to one
   D. Two to three tall

19. A good sequence has (1 mark)
   A. only jumps
   B. no order
   C. only noise
   D. a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish

20. In this lesson's sequence, what comes after the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Netball pass
   B. Lower the hips to the mat
   C. Sprint start
   D. Side roll immediately

21. In music, the sign p means (1 mark)
   A. loud
   B. fast
   C. stop
   D. soft

22. Which of these can also take digital photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Tablet
   B. Broom
   C. Drum
   D. Xylophone

23. The element of light means (1 mark)
   A. how well the subject is lit
   B. the weight of the camera
   C. the price
   D. the size of the photo

24. How should you hold the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   B. Above your head
   C. Pointing at your face
   D. Flat on your lap

25. If G is doh, then B is (1 mark)
   A. me
   B. doh
   C. ray
   D. soh

26. The descant recorder is played by (1 mark)
   A. plucking strings
   B. striking it
   C. shaking it
   D. blowing air into it

27. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the highest? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. G
   C. B
   D. A

28. What happens if you lift your head during a glide? (1 mark)
   A. Your legs sink
   B. You fly
   C. Nothing
   D. You go faster

29. Water games help learners to (1 mark)
   A. feel comfortable in the water
   B. avoid the pool
   C. forget to swim
   D. study more

30. In a glide, your face is (1 mark)
   A. high above the water
   B. in the water with the head between your arms
   C. turned to the side always
   D. hidden by a hat

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why is gymnastics not a race? (2 marks)

32. Why does a drum sound higher when its skin is tightened? (3 marks)

33. Describe the steps for painting a picture of one object that shows colour value. (5 marks)

34. Name four guide lines used for free hand lettering. (4 marks)

35. Explain how to prepare and perform a folk song with your class. (5 marks)

36. Give four ways in which gymnastics helps the body. (4 marks)

37. Why should we enter the water feet first? (2 marks)

38. Explain the meaning of diction and why it matters. (3 marks)

39. Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect. (4 marks)

40. Describe the roles of the soloist, the chorus and the instrumentalists in a folk song. (3 marks)

41. State four safety rules for gymnastics. (4 marks)

42. State three qualities of a good melody. (3 marks)

43. Explain how to make a tint of blue. (2 marks)

44. Explain how you would learn a simple melody on B, A and G. (4 marks)

45. What is the difference between a working portfolio and a display portfolio? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — By shaking it
   The kayamba is a shaker with seeds inside. You shake it back and forth.

2. D — To hold the skin tight
   Ropes or lacing keep the skin stretched tight.

3. C — Find the steady beat
   You must find the beat before you can add patterns.

4. A — It vibrates and makes the sound
   The stretched skin shakes very fast and produces sound.

5. B — how light or dark something is
   Tone is the lightness or darkness of a colour or shading.

6. D — 0.9 metres
   A defender must stand at least 0.9 metres away.

7. C — what the montage is about
   The subject matter is the theme.

8. D — Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   Clean-up shows responsibility.

9. A — silence
   A rest tells the performer to stay silent for a time.

10. D — taa
   Taa is the name for one long sound in one beat.

11. D — t
   The letter t is a tall letter, with a stem that rises above small letters.

12. B — aural work
   Aural work uses the ears to identify notes.

13. B — d to r
   Doh to ray is to the next note.

14. A — the land and natural wealth
   Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.

15. A — defence of freedom
   The shield and spears represent the defence of freedom.

16. C — green
   Green is at the bottom.

17. C — slow you down like a brake
   Leaning back acts like a brake.

18. A — Three to two
   A flag rectangle is about one and a half times as long as it is high.

19. D — a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish
   Good sequences are planned and controlled.

20. B — Lower the hips to the mat
   You lower the hips, lie straight, then roll.

21. D — soft
   The letter p stands for soft.

22. A — Tablet
   Many tablets have cameras.

23. A — how well the subject is lit
   Light is a key element.

24. A — Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   The recorder is held pointing down at about 45 degrees.

25. A — me
   G, A, B match d, r, m.

26. D — blowing air into it
   A recorder is a wind instrument that you blow.

27. C — B
   Fewer covered holes give a higher note.

28. A — Your legs sink
   Lifting the head lowers the legs.

29. A — feel comfortable in the water
   They build confidence.

30. B — in the water with the head between your arms
   Keeping the face in helps the body stay level.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is about control and quality of movement, not about speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for control, 1 mark for not speed.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: A tighter skin vibrates faster. Faster vibration makes a higher sound. Ropes are used to tighten the skin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for faster vibration, 1 mark for higher sound, 1 mark for the ropes or tightening.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose an object and place it near a window. Draw the outline lightly. Mix the main colour and paint the object. Add a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side. Blend the edges and add a shadow, then let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear steps.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a song and say the community, type and message. Share roles among soloist, chorus and instrumentalists. Practise pitch, rhythm, tempo and dynamics. Add gestures and expressions. Perform with respect and take a bow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing the song, roles, practising, expression and performing respectfully.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Makes muscles stronger; improves flexibility; improves balance and coordination; exercises the heart and lungs; builds confidence. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is safer because you cannot hit your head on the bottom, and you can see where you land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Diction is saying the words clearly. It matters because the audience can understand the message of the song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads, the chorus answers and repeats, the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a mat or soft ground; keep the space clear; remove jewellery; tie back long hair; warm up; take turns; stop if there is pain. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add white to blue, a little at a time, until it is as light as you want.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for white, 1 mark for adding gradually.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing it in sol-fa, clap and say the rhythm, finger the notes without blowing, play slowly, then speed up keeping the beat steady.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A working portfolio holds work in progress. A display portfolio holds the best finished works for showing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
